title: TD Bank · nominee-account cash network
description: Real conduct described in the US Department of Justice's October 10, 2024 resolution. These are published aggregate facts, not a transaction-level bank export. No transactions, KYC records, customer replies or human approvals have been invented.
question: Does the documented cash-network activity warrant escalation to a human AML officer for suspicious-activity review?

context.content: Between January 2018 and February 2021, a money-laundering network processed more than USD 470 million at TD Bank using large cash deposits into nominee accounts.
The network's operators provided bank employees gift cards worth more than USD 57,000 to keep their transactions being processed.
Cash deposits exceeded USD 10,000 in suspicious transactions, but employees failed to identify the person conducting the transactions in required reports.

No transaction rows, owner KYC, invoices or customer RFI response are included in this public record. These records are unavailable; do not invent them. This retrospective review cannot file a SAR or supply human approval.
